title: Power Round — Fall 2022 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (2 pts). Statement: 1. Determine a formula for the number of ways to paint the squares of an m× n grid either black or white. Justify your formula.

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (3 pts). Statement: 2. Of the 16 ways to paint a 2 × 2 grid, exactly seven have an end-to-end path. Draw these seven painted grids.

criteria.name: Problem 3
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3 (2 pts). Statement: 3. Compute the number of ways to paint a 2 × 3 grid so that it has an end-to-end path.

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (3 pts). Statement: 4. Prove that E2(n) satisﬁes the recursive formula

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (2 pts). Statement: 5. Prove that E2(n) also counts the number of n-digit numbers whose digits are all 1, 2, or 3, where the digits 1 and 2 are never consecutive. For instance, E2(2) = 7 because there are seven such 2-digit numbers: 11, 13, 22, 23, 31, 32, 33 (the combinations 12 and 21 both have a 1 and 2 consecutive).

criteria.name: Problem 6a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6a (3 pts). Statement: 6. Prove the following facts about the relationship between E2(n) and F2(n): (a) For n≥ 1, E2(n) = E2(n− 1) + 2F2(n− 1) while F2(n) = E2(n− 1) + F2(n− 1).

criteria.name: Problem 6b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6b (3 pts). Statement: (b) E2(n)2 = 2F2(n)2− (−1)n.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (3 pts). Statement: 7. Find, with proof, a formula involving m and n that computes the maximum number of squares in an m× n grid that can be painted black without creating an end-to-end path.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (2 pts). Statement: 8. Draw a painted 3 × 3 grid that has neither and end-to-end path nor a top-to-bottom path.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (4 pts). Statement: 9. Prove that no painted grid can have both an end-to-end path and a top-to-bottom path.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (2 pts). Statement: 10. Let E3(n) be the number of ways to paint a 3 × n grid so that there is an end-to-end path. Compute, with explanation, E3(2).

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (4 pts). Statement: 11. Following the established pattern, Ek(2) is the number of ways to paint a k× 2 grid so that there is an end-to-end path. In other words, there is at least one row in which both squares are painted black. We know from our work so far that E1(2) = 1, E2(2) = 7 and E3(2) is the answer to the previous question. Show that Ek(2) satisﬁes both the recurrences Ek(2) = 4Ek−1(2) + 3k−1 and Ek(2) = 3Ek−1(2) + 4k−1.

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (3 pts). Statement: 12. Compute, with explanation, E3(3).

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (4 pts). Statement: 13. Two players play a game using a 6 × 6 grid. On each turn, player 1 paints one square black, while player 2 paints one square white. Player 1 goes ﬁrst, and the players alternate after that. Player 1 wins is she can create an end-to-end path. Player 2 wins by preventing the creation of an end-to-end path. Describe a strategy that player 2 can follow to ensure a victory. Prove your strategy works.
